_comment: PB-71 (qa/parity-bindings.md): the 27 README + 29 CHANGELOG documented-
behaviour claims cross-checked in qa/evidence/inventory/1.5.5-ops-observability.md §8 (§8.3
one cross-check section apiece for README and for CHANGELOG). Every claim testable through the
binary has a `documented` family
cell in testing/shadow-oracle/cells.json (status: "cell", the `cell` field names it); the two
rows BUSBAR-1.6.0.md names CONTRADICTED get a cell that pins the CODE's actual behaviour
instead (status: "cell", `contradicted: true`). Claims that are pure prose — external
benchmarks, Docker/Kubernetes manifest literals busbar itself never observes, CI-pipeline-only
behaviour, Cargo/build metadata, or a bare pointer into another §'s own detailed cross-check —
are `status: "prose"` with a one-line `reason`, never silently dropped.
THIS FILE IS A REGISTER, NOT A GATE: it compares nothing on its own. The gate that asserts it is
`cargo xtask gate documented-claims`, which checks the
shape of every claim, that the claim run for each document is complete and contiguous, that the
`counts` block below is what the claims actually add up to, that every `cell` id named here exists
in testing/shadow-oracle/cells.json AND was RECORDED PASS by the pinned golden, and that both
CONTRADICTED rows stay flagged, cell-pinned, and carry the behaviour the code actually has.
`quote` is the 1.5.5 inventory's text. The documents customers read are the LIVE README.md and
CHANGELOG.md, which have been reworded since: a claim therefore carries `live`, the live
document's own wording of it (the gate finds every `live` fragment word for word in the document
its id names), or `gone`, the reason the live document no longer makes it (the gate refuses
`gone` while the live document still carries the quote). A claim with neither must have its
`quote` in the live document as written.
An earlier version of this note claimed the design-bindings gate verified the `cell` ids.
It did not: nothing in the tree opened this file at all.
